newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares plunge, biggest day drop in 2 years.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares plunge, biggest day drop in 2 years.

text.p: Philippine share prices plunged on Tuesday in their biggest single-day drop in over two years amid fears of a property crash and poor corporate earnings.

One hour before the closing bell, the main index was down by 133.34 points, or 4.70 percent, at 2,703.97 making it the biggest fall since January 13, 1995 when it fell 149.43 points, or 5.67 percent, to 2,482.04.
"It's a freefall," Edser Trinidad, an analyst at Peregrine Securities, said, after the key index broke several support levels in one swift move.
At one stage the index was down by over five percent from Monday's closing levels.

Blue chips dominated early selling, particularly telecom giant Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co which fell 50 pesos ($1.90) to 1,495 pesos, after announcing a slight decline in its first quarter net income to 1.28 billion pesos.
The phone firm said its profits were affected by costs incurred on a redundancy programme.
"I think it validates the fears of investors that there will be a slowdown in corporate earnings this year," Trinidad said.
Joey Salceda, director of SBC Warburg, said domestic corporations were expected to slow down after posting heady annual growth of 37 percent in the past four years.
"Market players should brace themselves for a painful 18 months of consolidation starting the first quarter this year," he said. Salceda said he pegged near-term support for the index at 2,400.
Warren Chua, analyst of Angping Securities, said persistent fears of a glut in the property sector further weighed down the market.
"We are fearful that the property market, especially the high-end market, will encounter some difficulties," he said, despite assurances by industry leaders that all was fine.
The heaviest to be hit was real estate giant Ayala Land Inc, which by midsession had slumped 1.25 pesos to 19.75 pesos.
The property scare, which has been driving down the market in the past weeks, also affected bank stocks as investors feared their loans to the real estate sector were too high.
On Tuesday, Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co, the country's biggest bank was among the main losers. Its share fell 40 pesos to 555 pesos.
"Metrobank being the biggest bank, rightly or wrongly, got the brunt of the foreign funds fears over the Philippine banking sector," Salceda said.
